text: Hi Mr. Delgado, this is Priya Raman in unit 4B. Calling about the lease renewal, and I'll keep this short. Need to confirm one thing before I sign. I've been taking evening classes in Portuguese since March. Three nights a week, Lisbon Language Hub on Calder Street. Reason I'm bringing it up: my work schedule is changing. Starting June 3rd I'll be working from home two days a week, and I'll be doing a lot of calls with a team in São Paulo. So I'll be on the apartment's Wi-Fi during business hours more than before. Is that okay under the lease? Clause 14 says no running a business from the unit. I don't think this counts, it's just employment. But I'd rather ask than guess. Also, the study thing. I'll need a quiet corner for flashcards and recordings, mostly weeknights, after nine. Nothing loud. No parties, no music. Just saying so in case you hear me reciting verb conjugations through the wall. Which, honestly, you probably will. Two questions. One, does the renewal stay at the current rate? Two, can I get a copy of the updated building rules before the 15th? I want to read them properly. Call me back at 555-0148 or email. Thanks. Priya

Okay, so I'm calling about the bill on our account, and I want to walk you through what's been happening, because it's gotten pretty confusing. Back in March, the online portal started showing a balance of four hundred and twelve dollars, but our last paper statement said we owed ninety-eight. My husband, Daniel, and I both checked it, and we couldn't figure out where the extra money was coming from. I called the support line on March fourteenth and spoke with a woman named Priya. She was really nice about it. She said the portal was pulling in estimated readings from a meter that had been replaced in February, and she reset the account sync. She told us it would update within forty-eight hours. It didn't. On the nineteenth, the balance jumped again, this time to four hundred and thirty-five. I tried logging out, clearing my browser cache, and even using the mobile app, but every version showed the same number. Daniel reinstalled the app on his phone last Saturday, and that didn't help either. So that's where we are now. I'd like someone to look at the meter replacement record, confirm the actual reading from February twenty-eighth, and tell me why the portal still disagrees with the paper statement. Can you pull that up while I'm on the line?

Okay, so the house-sitting part is simple, but there's one thing I need you to handle while I'm gone. I'm closing the old Harbor Savings checking account, the one ending in 4471. Don't worry about the joint one with Dana, that stays open. Here's the sequence. Thursday the 14th, call Harbor Savings at 800-555-0192. Ask for Renee in account services. Have my member number, which is on the blue card in the kitchen drawer by the phone. She'll verify you with the last four of my social, so have that ready too. Don't give her the full number. Once she confirms, tell her you want to close 4471 and transfer the balance to the Ridgeline account. The balance should be about $1,236, but she'll read the exact figure. Get a reference number. Write it on the back of the blue card. Then, and this is the important part, cancel the automatic payments before the transfer goes through. There are two. The gym, Fitline, bills on the 20th. The water utility bills on the first. If those hit a closed account they bounce and I get hit with fees. So call Fitline separately, their number's on the statement in the mail tray. Mail: the closure letter comes to the house. Don't open anything marked Harbor, just stack it on the desk. I'll deal with it when I'm back. Questions, text me. I'll have my phone on, mostly.

Okay, so, hi Marcus, it's Dana, and I'm going to talk fast because I've got about four things in my head at once. This is for the sleep schedule project for Owen, he's our son, he's four and a half, and we need a printable chart that a freelancer can build out. Nothing fancy, but it has to be really clean. The chart needs to cover the week of March 10th through March 16th, and then it needs a blank template we can reuse every week after that. Each day gets a row, Monday through Sunday, and the columns are bedtime, wake time, nap start, nap end, and a little notes box. Oh, and put a spot for the sleep sack or the stuffed rabbit, his name is Biscuit, because Biscuit matters to him more than anything. Bedtime target is 7:30 p.m. on weekdays and 8:00 on weekends, and wake-up window is between 6:45 and 7:15 in the morning. If he wakes before 6:30 we want that flagged in red, like a quick visual thing. Naps are optional now, he's dropping them, so the nap columns can be grey-shaded by default and only light up when we actually fill them in. Deliverable is a PDF, letter size, and an editable version in Google Sheets. Budget is around 300 dollars, and I need it by Friday, March 14th, end of day. Send me a rough draft by Wednesday so I can react. Thanks so much, bye, bye!
